article_content: Washington (CNN) -- As the Senate casts its first round of votes on immigration reform this week, a divided Republican conference in the House may be a roadblock to any immigration measure passing Congress this year. House Speaker John Boehner faces a critical test due to the internal split within the Republican party. During a closed meeting last week, two Senate GOP "Gang of Eight" members -- Marco Rubio and Jeff Flake -- faced over 100 Republican members of the conservative Republican Study Committee (RSC). Alabama GOP Rep. Mo Brooks said those senators explaining the merits of the plan "were doing their best to put lipstick on a pig." Georgia Rep. Tom Price, a leading conservative, said it was "highly unlikely" the majority of House Republicans would vote for a bill similar to the Senate deal. There is a bloc of House GOP members, including Rep. Paul Ryan, pushing for a bipartisan approach similar to the Senate's plan, which includes a path to citizenship. Rep. Raul Labrador dropped out of the House bipartisan immigration group, citing frustration over not getting support for his detailed proposal on undocumented workers' access to taxpayer-funded health care benefits. House Judiciary Committee Chairman Bob Goodlatte disagrees with the Senate Democrats' strategy, preferring to move discrete immigration measures through his committee. Boehner is careful not to signal whether he will move immigration in one package or allow votes on separate bills, stressing that any legislation would follow "regular order."

Huis Speaker John Boehner staar 'n kritieke toets in die gesig as gevolg van die interne verdeeldheid binne die Republikeinse party. Tydens 'n geslote vergadering verlede week het twee Senaat GOP "Gang of Eight" lede -- Marco Rubio en Jeff Flake -- meer as 100 Republikeinse lede van die konserwatiewe Republikeinse Studiekomitee (RSK) gekonfronteer. Alabama GOP Rep. Mo Brooks het gesê dat die senatore wat die plan se meriete verduidelik het "hulle beste gedoen het om lipstiffie op 'n vark te sit." Georgia Rep. Tom Price, 'n leidende konserwatief, het gesê dit is "hoogs onwaarskynlik" dat die meerderheid van die Huis Republikeine sou stem vir 'n wetsontwerp soortgelyk aan die Senaat se ooreenkoms. Daar is 'n blok Huis GOP lede, insluitend Rep. Paul Ryan, wat 'n tweepartydige benadering soortgelyk aan die Senaat se plan, wat 'n pad na burgerskap insluit, steun. Rep. Raul Labrador het uit die Huis se tweepartydige immigrasiegroep getree en frustrasie uitgespreek oor die gebrek aan ondersteuning vir sy gedetailleerde voorstel oor ongedokumenteerde werkers se toegang tot belastingbetaler-gefinansierde gesondheidsorgvoordele. Huis Regterlike Komitee Voorsitter Bob Goodlatte verskil met die Senaat Demokrate se strategie en verkies om diskrete immigrasiewetgewing deur sy komitee te beweeg. Boehner is versigtig om nie te sinspeel of hy immigrasiestappe in een pakket sal beweeg of stemme oor afsonderlike wette sal toelaat nie, en beklemtoon dat enige wetgewing "gereelde orde" sal volg.

Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan highlighted future security challenges driven by global geopolitics and technology.

Bloys forwarded VanArendonk's tweet to Kathleen McCaffrey, HBO's senior vice president of drama programming, suggesting that a 'Twitter user should tweet that that's a pretty blithe response to what soldiers legitimately go through on [the] battlefield.' article_content: A recent study by the Spanish Scientific Research Council (CSIC) has identified between 129 and 221 new species of frogs in Madagascar. The findings suggest that the number of amphibian species on the island has been significantly underestimated. 'The diversity of species in Madagascar is far from being known,' said Professor David R. Vieites. 'Our data suggest that the number of new species of amphibians is spatially widespread, even in well-studied areas.' The study highlights that Madagascar's biodiversity could be much higher than previously thought, with important implications for conservation planning.

'Ons data toon dat die aantal nuwe amfibiese spesies wydverspreid is, selfs in gebiede wat goed bestudeer is.' article_content: The only existing self-portrait by Leonardo da Vinci will be displayed in Turin, Italy, as part of an exhibition titled 'Leonardo and the treasures of the king'. The exhibition will run for two and a half months at the Royal Library, starting on Thursday. The self-portrait, a fragile chalk sketch, has been publicly displayed only three times in the last century. According to Italian lore, Leonardo's gaze is intensely strengthening for those who view it. During World War II, it was moved to Rome to prevent the Nazis from exploiting its supposed supernatural qualities. The library's director, Giovanni Saccani, confirmed that an intelligence operation was used to transport it to Rome. The exhibition will feature 80 masterpieces from the Royal Library, which was founded in 1839 by Charles Albert and is now a UNESCO World Heritage site. The library houses 4,500 manuscripts, 1,500 parchments, and over 3,000 drawings by famous artists. Works by Raphael, Carrache, Rembrandt, and Anthony van Dyck will be included, along with various manuscripts. Visitors are required to reserve tickets, with limited admission.

Die selfportret, 'n kwetsbare kryttekening, word selde vertoon. Volgens Italiaanse oorlewering het Leonardo se blik 'n versterkende effek op die kyker. Tydens die Tweede Wêreldoorlog is die selfportret na Rome verskuif om te verhoed dat die Nazi's dit sou uitbuit. Die uitstalling sal 80 meesterwerke uit die Koninklike Biblioteek bevat, wat 'n UNESCO-wêrelderfenisgebied is. Werke deur verskeie bekende kunstenaars sal vertoon word, insluitend Raphael, Rembrandt, en Anthony van Dyck. Besoekers moet kaartjies vooraf bespreek weens beperkte toelating.

article_content: Washington (CNN) -- Actor and comedian Will Ferrell was awarded the prestigious Mark Twain Prize for American Humor by the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts on Sunday night. The award, established in 1998, honors comedians who have shaped American society with their work, just as Mark Twain once did. Ferrell told CNN it's 'the only legitimate award that recognizes comedy,' and he was honored to receive it. Fellow comedians Jack Black, Tim Meadows, Ed Asner, Paul Rudd, Andy Samberg, Conan O'Brien, and Molly Shannon praised Ferrell at the ceremony. 'When you see Will Ferrell on a marquee, he's going to give you 90 minutes to two hours of fascinating entertainment,' said Asner, who worked with Ferrell in the movie 'Elf.' In 'Elf,' Will 'was so steeped in his character that I had to believe in mine,' Asner said. 'He's a blast. I mean, he's always coming up with new stuff,' said actor Rudd, who co-starred with Ferrell in 'Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy.' O'Brien took a different approach -- the backhanded compliment. 'None of us are here for Will,' he said. 'We're here because Will's very powerful. We fear Will. Let's get that straight, okay? I'm angry. And afraid. I'm here out of fear.' Senior administration officials, including White House Chief of Staff William Daley, Transportation Secretary Ray LaHood, Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius, and Office of Management and Budget Director Jacob Lew, were also in attendance.

Kennedy-sentrum vir die Uitvoerende Kunste toegeken. Die toekenning, wat in 1998 ingestel is, eer komediante wat Amerikaanse samelewing met hul werk gevorm het, net soos Mark Twain dit eens gedoen het. Ferrell het aan CNN gesê dit is 'die enigste wettige toekenning wat komedie erken,' en hy was vereer om dit te ontvang. Mede-komediants Jack Black, Tim Meadows, Ed Asner, Paul Rudd, Andy Samberg, Conan O'Brien, en Molly Shannon het Ferrell by die seremonie geprys. In 'Elf' was Will 'so vasgevang in sy karakter dat ek in myne moes glo,' het Asner gesê. 'Hy's 'n groot pret. He told CNN that his family wasn't at home during the attack and that he'd never received threats before. article_content: Djimon Hounsou's journey to stardom is truly astonishing. Born in Benin, he faced significant hardship in his early life, scavenging for food and sleeping on the streets. However, he rose to become an international fashion model and a Hollywood star, appearing in films like 'Gladiator,' 'Amistad,' and 'Blood Diamond.' He worked with renowned directors like Steven Spielberg and actors like Leonardo DiCaprio. Hounsou's role in 'In America' made him the first black African man to be nominated for an Oscar. He continued to impress with his performance in 'Blood Diamond,' earning a second Oscar nomination. Growing up without his parents in Benin and later facing challenges in Paris, Hounsou's early life was marked by loneliness and hardship. However, his fortunes changed when he was discovered by a Paris photographer and began his career as a fashion model under Thierry Mugler. This opportunity led him to the United States, where he pursued his dream of becoming an actor. Hounsou's breakthrough came with 'Amistad,' directed by Steven Spielberg. He has since appeared in significant roles, including in 'Blood Diamond,' a film set during Sierra Leone's civil war. Apart from his acting career, Hounsou is an activist, particularly in the fight against climate change, and has worked with charities like Oxfam and SOS. In 2009, he spoke at the United Nations' Summit on Climate Change. Despite his achievements, Hounsou feels he is just beginning his journey.

article_content: Magnus MacFarlane-Barrow was enjoying a pint at his local pub in the Scottish Highlands when he got an idea that would change his life -- and the lives of thousands of others. It was 1992, and MacFarlane-Barrow and his brother Fergus had just seen a news report about refugee camps in Bosnia. The images shocked the two salmon farmers, who'd visited Bosnia as teenagers and remembered the warmth of the Bosnian people. 'We began saying 'Wouldn't it be wonderful if we could just do one small thing to help?' ' MacFarlane-Barrow says. After talking it over, the two men took a week off work, collected food, clothing, medicine, and blankets, loaded everything into an old Land Rover, and drove to Bosnia to deliver it. 'I came back thinking I'd done my one good deed, but it didn't work out like that,' he says. Upon returning home, the brothers found an 'avalanche of goods' that people had continued to donate while they were away. 'I was touched by the overwhelming generosity of others,' MacFarlane-Barrow remembers. 'I saw all those donations in our family home and thought, 'Wow, people really are good,' and it inspired me to be good too.' After much thought and prayer, Magnus MacFarlane-Barrow quit his job, sold his home, and dedicated himself to helping people in need. He returned to Bosnia 22 more times during the Bosnian War, and over the next 18 years, his work expanded. Today, his program -- Mary's Meals -- provides free daily meals to more than 400,000 children worldwide. MacFarlane-Barrow found his current focus in 2002 while working in Malawi, where he met a local teenager who wanted a decent meal and an education. 'The mother of the family was dying of AIDS. She was lying on her bare mud floor with her six children around her,' he says. 'I started talking to her oldest child, Edward. And Edward said, 'I'd like to have enough food to eat. I'd like to go to school one day.' ' In response, he launched Mary's Meals, aiming to break the cycle of poverty by feeding children a daily meal at school. The food gives students an incentive to continue their schooling and helps them focus better. 'Pass rates go up dramatically in schools where we start providing Mary's Meals,' he says. Mary's Meals partners with local residents, who handle the daily work of cooking and serving food. In Malawi, over 10,000 volunteers donate their time regularly. The program operates in over 500 schools and child-care facilities in 15 countries. MacFarlane-Barrow coordinates the global effort from a tin shed on his parents' property in Scotland. 'I see the children's faces as they eat their meal,' he says. 'Knowing I can transform their lives keeps me motivated.' Mary's Meals has faced new challenges, such as in Haiti after the earthquake, where they expanded their mission to include temporary classrooms and rebuilding schools. MacFarlane-Barrow is driven by his Christian faith, but there's no ministry aspect to his work. 'We serve those in need... period.' 'When I think of Mary's Meals, I think of it as a series of lots and lots of little acts of love,' he says.

article_content: A recent spate of unusual weather hasn't changed the question on many people's minds - 'what about a white Christmas?' While snow is possible in the northern US, most areas won't see significant accumulation. The Northeast has little chance of a white Christmas due to recent warm temperatures and rain, with areas affected by lake-effect snow being an exception. The mid-Atlantic and southeast US also have virtually no chance of snow. In contrast, the northern Great Lakes are likely to have a white Christmas, with snow forecast for Christmas Day. The northern central US is already buried under snow and ice, and this is expected to continue. The West Coast, as usual, won't have a white Christmas, but will enjoy good weather. Parts of the Southwest may see snow, but this will be limited to higher elevations.
